newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela out of S.Africa hospital after surgery.
newsitem.headline: Mandela out of S.Africa hospital after surgery.

text.p: President Nelson Mandela was discharged from a South African military hospital on Sunday after undergoing a minor knee operation at the weekend, his spokesman said.
"The president left hospital this morning. He's okay. Everything went well," presidential spokesman Parks Mankahlana told Reuters.
Mandela was admitted to the 1st Military Hospital in Pretoria on Saturday to undergo surgery on his right knee.
Mankahlana said he had recurring problems with his knee as a result of an injury sustained during his 27 years in prison.
He said there was no need for concern over the president's health, adding Mandela would resume his official duties without delay.
"He will continue as usual," Mankahlana said.
Mandela's record as the man who led South Africa's peaceful change from apartheid to democracy has led many foreign and domestic investors to regard him as essential to the country's stability.
To quell doubts about what will happen when he retires as head of state in 1999, Mandela, now 78, has endorsed Deputy President Thabo Mbeki as his successor.
